missing.what: Flux reinstalls the release when the chart name changes. The plan's nameOverride and lookup guard do not cover this.
missing.where: deploy/flux/app/helmrelease.yaml (no spec.upgrade.chartNameChangeStrategy), deploy/helm/warp/Chart.yaml name: warp -> humagen (plan 2.9.1 and 2.9.8)
missing.why: In fluxcd/helm-controller (internal/controller/helmrelease_controller.go:383, action.ReleaseTargetChanged, verified in its source), a changed chart name makes the controller uninstall the current release and install it again. The default is Upgrade.GetChartNameChangeStrategy() == Reinstall, and older controllers do this unconditionally. As a result the Deployment, Service, ConfigMap and Ingress are deleted, so there is downtime. Guard 2.9.3 looks up a Deployment that has already been deleted, so it never fires: a cluster that forgot nameOverride comes back as warp-humagen with a new empty PVC. The old PVC survives only because of helm.sh/resource-policy: keep (pvc.yaml:10). Guard 2.9.4 fails after the uninstall, so the app stays down. Fix: set upgrade.chartNameChangeStrategy: InPlaceUpdate in helmrelease.yaml and in the docs for copied app/ dirs, or treat Chart.yaml name: warp as a kept tier-2 identity. Add a Flux reconcile to the kind test in section 7.

missing.what: The deploy paths read spec-named variables by exact name, and AdoptEnv copies only from old to new
missing.where: internal/app/deploy.go:572 applySecret os.Getenv(v); deploy.go:331 env[v] = "${"+v+":-}" in generated compose; carry() deploy.go:180-186 passes env:NAME through
missing.why: A spec that still says env:WARP_X, on a shell where the operator renamed the variable to HUMAGEN_X as the note tells them, breaks two ways. Kubernetes deploy fails with 'the spec references WARP_X, which this shell has not set'. Compose interpolates an empty value. The same applies to renamed WARP_REF_n for `deploy -o` users whose own env or CI supplies the values: generated compose has no env_file, so the old name never reaches the container. Use legacy.LookupEnv in applySecret and write `${X:-${OTHER:-}}` in generated compose.

missing.what: Exact-name grants and person starts are tied to the prefix of stored refs. The overlap check does not treat WARP_ and HUMAGEN_ as the same.
missing.where: internal/platform/clients.go:284 slices.Contains(SecretRefs[tenant], name); pkg/credentials/starts.go CheckStart, CheckStarts and Owns
missing.why: Following the rename note breaks stored data. Renaming a -secret-refs or secret_env grant to HUMAGEN_X stops every stored client ref env:WARP_X. Renaming a person_refs start to env:HUMAGEN_PERSON_{subject}_ (or keychain:humagen-people-… as the bulk-renamed docs/spec.md:103 suggests) makes every stored person ref no longer 'owned'. CheckStarts also lets tenant A use env:WARP_PERSON_{subject}_ and tenant B use env:HUMAGEN_PERSON_{subject}_. AdoptEnv and LookupEnv then make B's ana read A's ana's credential, which breaks the 'no reference under two people' invariant. Normalise the prefix in grant matching, Owns, Expand and CheckStarts, and do not tell people to rename refs that stored data names.

wrong.claim: 2.4: an unexported old field with json:"warp_client" lets the strict decoder (spec.go:230) keep accepting old files
wrong.truth: encoding/json ignores unexported fields. With DisallowUnknownFields every old spec fails with `json: unknown field "warp_client"` (checked with a Go snippet). The old field must be exported, cleared after decode, and marked omitempty.

wrong.claim: 2.9.4: when the image guard fails, the render fails and the running release stays
wrong.truth: Under Flux, helm-controller first uninstalls the release because the chart name changed (default Reinstall strategy). The failed render then leaves nothing running.

wrong.claim: No word in the repo contains warp other than the product's own names, so a case-preserving replace is safe once the kept names are protected
wrong.truth: The protect regexes match code (this.warp.connections, config.warp.client). The case-sensitive keep misses Warp-Writer and WARP-WRITER, and `_warp.sources` slips past \b. The dry run gives 3 TS errors, 1 Slack test failure and 1 Go test failure, plus the render-slack length assertion.

wrong.claim: 2.2: after AdoptEnv, each of the ~14 raw reads (including deploy.go:572) needs nothing more than its constant changed
wrong.truth: deploy.go:572 and the generated compose read whatever variable the spec's ref names, which is user data. They need LookupEnv or nested interpolation.

wrong.claim: 2.5: WARP_REF_n is renamed with no compat because every deploy regenerates all three places, so a stale key is harmless
wrong.truth: With `deploy -o`, the user supplies the values from their own env or CI. Generated compose then passes an empty HUMAGEN_REF_n into the container.

wrong.claim: 2.2: the overlap rule in CheckStarts is unchanged
wrong.truth: With two accepted prefixes and two-way LookupEnv, the rule must compare starts with the prefix normalised. Otherwise starts in two tenants can name one secret.

wrong.claim: 2.9.7: setting nameOverride when `helm list` shows a warp-* chart is enough for humagen deploy
wrong.truth: That works only for the first upgrade. Later deploys see humagen-* and fail the guard.
